external_entities.name: player
external_entities.description: A player who runs the game client on a machine they control and plays the game.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Players run our game client on their own machines. We do not control those machines.

external_entities.name: customer support staff
external_entities.description: Staff who work from the corporate network and use the moderation website to act on player accounts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: our customer support staff work from the corporate network and use a moderation website

processes.name: game client
processes.description: The client players launch and use to play the game.
processes.source_excerpt: The player launches the client and plays through it.

processes.name: lobby
processes.description: The production-network service used for matchmaking and match setup.
processes.source_excerpt: It talks to the lobby on TCP 1234 for matchmaking

processes.name: game server
processes.description: The production-network service that handles matches and updates player and stats data.
processes.source_excerpt: once a match starts it talks directly to the game servers on TCP 1235

processes.name: moderation website
processes.description: The website customer support staff use to look at and act on player accounts.
processes.source_excerpt: use a moderation website to look at and act on player accounts

trust_boundaries.name: player machines
trust_boundaries.description: Machines owned or controlled by players, outside the system operator's control.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Players run our game client on their own machines. We do not control those machines.

trust_boundaries.name: production network
trust_boundaries.description: The production network containing the lobby, game servers, and databases.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: two things in our production network

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which customer support staff use the moderation website.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: our customer support staff work from the corporate network

assumptions.assumption: The lobby is internet-facing because it must be reachable from wherever a player is and is described as exposed.
assumptions.basis: The lobby is exposed and must be reachable from wherever a player is.

assumptions.assumption: The game server is internet-facing because it must be reachable from wherever a player is and is described as exposed.
assumptions.basis: The game servers are exposed and must be reachable from wherever a player is.

assumptions.assumption: Player machines form a tenant boundary because the players control those machines and the system operator does not.
assumptions.basis: The text says players run the client on their own machines and that those machines are not controlled by the system operator.

assumptions.assumption: The production network is a network boundary because it is a distinct network location containing production services.
assumptions.basis: The text explicitly distinguishes the production network from player machines and the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The corporate network is a network boundary because it is a distinct network location used by customer support staff.
assumptions.basis: The text explicitly distinguishes the corporate network from the production network and player machines.
